tested_scope: One bounded GitHub public-fork witness authority classification using current own Part86 continuation and official public GitHub documentation only. Tested whether a public fork can retain a minimum-generation/incarnation witness across target deletion/transfer and whether that yields a scheduled-Chat-native anti-rollback authority without a second principal, protected/manual setup, finite monthly/trial/paid quota or incremental monetary cost. No O, downstream, other-worker state/config/receipt, shared ledger, or legacy semantic input was read.

public_sources.observation: GitHub Enterprise Cloud documents that repository/fork deletion requires repository admin or organization-owner authority and that deleting a public repository does not delete its forks.

GitHub.com documentation states that if a transferred repository has forks, those forks remain associated with the repository after transfer; owner/name reuse and transfer have additional constraints, so logical owner/name alone is not a sufficient incarnation proof.

GitHub documents that an admin of a public fork can permanently leave the fork network; commit metadata is preserved, while the resulting repository becomes standalone. The same page states people with admin access for a forked repository can delete that forked repository.

public_sources.source_scope: GitHub Enterprise Server 3.17 public-fork permission reference; used only as GitHub-family mechanism evidence, not as an unqualified GitHub.com guarantee.
public_sources.observation: The reference states public forks do not inherit the upstream permission structure. This supports the mechanism possibility that an independently administered public fork can separate target-admin authority, but this run does not elevate that version-specific text into a universal GitHub.com guarantee.

public_sources.observation_from_part86_own_state: GitHub Contents create/update requires write permission for repository contents. Therefore a Chat writer that is not authorized to the independently owned fork cannot maintain the witness; granting that authorization is a separate authority/setup event.

authority_matrix.reason: Public-fork survival after upstream deletion changes storage survival but not rollback authority. The same principal that administers the fork can delete it; therefore the witness is not outside the target principal's rollback domain.

A public fork can survive upstream deletion, so an independently administered fork can preserve witness material against target-repository deletion. However its independent owner/admin is now the anti-rollback trust anchor, which is a separate principal/protected authority outside the scheduled-Chat role.
The witness cannot advance without write authorization to that fork. Obtaining or expanding that authorization is not a role-local scheduled-Chat effect in the tested scope.

Least-privilege Contents-write can in principle separate writer mutation from repository-admin deletion authority, but the independent owner, permission grant and continuing protection must already exist or be established externally. That residual setup/principal dependency fails current Phase-1 acceptance.

Official transfer documentation says forks remain associated after transfer. A witness must still bind a target incarnation rather than owner/name alone; association continuity does not by itself prove anti-recreation identity.

The old public fork may survive target deletion, but a newly created repository at the old logical name is a distinct authority episode. The witness must carry an incarnation identifier established before deletion; this leaf does not claim a GitHub-provided identifier with a documented no-reuse anti-rollback guarantee.

Detachment can preserve commit metadata while severing fork-network association, and repository transfer can preserve fork association. These operations show network membership is not a stable authority identity. The fork's own admin domain remains able to delete or administratively transform the witness surface.

Repository-level branch/ruleset policy does not eliminate the repository administrator as rollback/deletion authority. The Part86 source-qualified result already showed repository admins can mutate/delete rulesets and repositories.

observation_vs_inference.observed: Official GitHub documentation establishes public-fork survival after public-upstream deletion, repository-admin deletion authority, fork detachment by fork admins with commit metadata preserved, fork association surviving transfer, and Contents-write requiring authorization to the repository being written.
observation_vs_inference.inference: A public fork is useful as a target-deletion-surviving copy, but it becomes an anti-target-rollback witness only when its administrative domain is genuinely independent. That independence is itself a second-principal/protected setup dependency unless already provided by a trusted external authority. Fork-network membership is also not a sufficient incarnation identity because transfer/detachment can change relationship metadata while preserving repository content.

leaf_result.new_falsification: Public-fork survivability does not remove the authority-separation requirement. Same-principal forks fail immediately; independently owned forks can survive target deletion and plausibly separate target-admin control, but then the independent owner/protection/authorization lifecycle is the anti-rollback root of trust and remains outside scheduled-Chat-native authority.
leaf_result.narrowed_positive: An independently administered public fork with a Chat writer holding only repository Contents-write, plus a durable incarnation binding, is a stronger architecture against target-repository deletion/rewind than a same-principal second repository. This is not accepted because the independent owner/admin and authorization grant are residual external/protected setup dependencies.
leaf_result.minimal_unresolved_child: A provider- or protocol-enforced monotonic witness whose rollback protection does not depend on a second administrator/principal and whose Chat write authorization plus target-incarnation binding can be created, recovered and rotated entirely inside the recurring scheduled-Chat authority domain at zero incremental cost and zero finite monthly/trial/paid quota.

quota_cost_dependency_assessment.rate_limit_note: Repository API rate limits remain a transport interruption to checkpoint around; they are not used as compute and are not treated as a passing authority mechanism.
quota_cost_dependency_assessment.residual_richer_mode_protected_manual_ex: present for the independent-fork variant because an independent owner/admin domain and writer authorization must pre-exist or be established outside the role-local scheduled-Chat authority

conflict_check: Exactly one bounded Part87 semantic leaf executed after durable presemantic witness. No optional second leaf, scheduler mutation, wait/poll/backoff, forbidden semantic read, shared ledger access, or cross-role state use.
continuation: Part88: execute exactly one bounded provider-retained Git-object witness leaf using official GitHub documentation plus own clean state only. Test whether a content-addressed commit/tree/blob in a public fork network can act as a minimum-generation/incarnation witness even after branch rewind or one repository/fork deletion, without requiring any independently administered repository. Required negatives: all repositories in the network deleted, fork network becomes empty, unreachable-object retention/garbage collection not documented, commit SHA discoverability after own-state rollback, force-push/ref deletion, upstream delete/recreate, and API/rate-limit interruption. Accept only if provider-enforced retention and discoverability are documented strongly enough that no second principal, richer/protected/manual step, finite monthly/trial/paid quota or incremental cost remains; otherwise persist the exact retention/discoverability gap.
